fact: One of the sky's loveliest double stars — a golden sun paired with a blue one.
bio: Almach (Gamma Andromedae) is a multiple system about 350 light-years away, celebrated for the vivid colour contrast between its bright golden-orange giant and a bluish companion — itself a triple — making it a favourite target for small telescopes.
cultural: The name derives from an Arabic term for a small desert cat or lynx. Almach marks the foot of the chained princess Andromeda, at the far end of the constellation from her head at Alpheratz.
